title: Timeline: the clock becoming synchronized and stepping evaluates; an unsynchronized start goes as without a timeline
description: The pump of case 75 (06:00 on, 08:00 off, ...), off with an exit action that logs. Booted at 07:00 without a synchronized clock, the rule takes initialState off with its entry action. The synchronization at 07:01 is an evaluation while the rule runs: a transition to on (exit actions of off, entry actions of on). The clock loses its synchronization, and a reboot then restores the persisted state on without entry actions; the synchronization at 07:04 evaluates again: a self-transition into on, which sends again. A step of the wall clock back by 30 s is no jump and changes nothing; a step forward by an hour (to 08:05:30) is one: the due state is off, entered by a transition, and the point 08:00 stepped over is not applied on its own; the step back by an hour evaluates again (on). The point 08:00 then applies when the clock reaches it (the wall clock is 30 s behind the start plus the monotonic time).
note: Decided 17: an evaluation while the rule runs is a transition (exit and entry actions); a jump is a step of more than 60 s (spec/rules.md 7.13).
